Chapter 8: Cultivating Self-Trust and Intuitive Decision-Making
Now that you’ve started to shift your inner story, the next step is all about building self-trust and learning how to make choices using your own intuition.
Self-trust is that quiet sense of confidence—the feeling that, no matter what comes up, you’ll be able to handle it. It’s knowing that your own feelings and perceptions really do matter.
Think of cultivating self-trust like tending a garden. It takes patience, care, and a willingness to listen to those subtle signals inside yourself. Sometimes, it’s as simple as noticing when something doesn’t feel quite right—like when someone’s words don’t match their actions. Other times, you might feel an unexpected sense of calm, especially in relationships where things are truly mutual.
So, how do you actually nurture self-trust in your daily life? Here are a few ideas:
First, make a habit of checking in with yourself. Instead of focusing on how a relationship “should” feel, ask yourself how it actually feels to you.
Second, honor those gut instincts—even if they’re inconvenient or a little uncomfortable. Your intuition is there for a reason.
Third, look back at times when your intuition was spot on. Remember those moments to reinforce your confidence in your own judgment.
And finally, give yourself permission to make mistakes. Each one is a chance to learn, not a sign that you’ve failed.
Here’s a real-world example: imagine someone who, after years of brushing off red flags, finally decides to listen to that uneasy feeling and step back from a new relationship that just doesn’t feel right. Even though it’s tough, this act of self-trust lays the foundation for healthier choices down the line.
Little by little, intuitive decision-making becomes almost second nature. You’ll find it brings more ease and flow into your relationships, and you’ll spend a lot less time overthinking or seeking outside approval.
